metadata.name: lattice_equities
metadata.description: Sealed batch auctions for tokenized stocks, cleared on Arcium

instructions.name: cancel_order
docs: Pulls a live order out before the clear and refunds its deposit. The order
stays in the encrypted book, but its slot is marked cancelled, and the clear
treats cancelled slots as size zero, so it can never fill.

instructions.name: clear_batch
docs: Queues `clear` with the Pyth-derived band. The band is public; the book is not.

accounts.name: price_update
docs: discriminator, verification level and feed are checked in the handler.

accounts.name: fallback_update
docs: only used when the primary price shows the exchange is closed.

instructions.name: expire_pending
docs: Releases a book stuck waiting on a computation that never returned. Anyone
can call it once the book's timeout has passed: a stuck order becomes
refundable, a stuck clear reopens the book, a stuck setup marks it dead.

accounts.name: ticket
docs: The pending order's ticket, required when the book is waiting on an order.

instructions.name: refund_failed_order
docs: Returns the deposit of an order whose encrypted computation failed, and
closes its ticket back to the trader.

instructions.name: settle_order
docs: Pays out one order after the clear and closes its ticket. Anyone can call it,
but funds only go to the ticket's trader. A buyer gets base lots plus unspent
quote back; a seller gets quote plus unsold base back. No cross: full refund.

instructions.name: submit_order
docs: Queues `place_order` with the trader's encrypted order and the current book.
Only one order is in flight at a time, so each computation sees the latest book.

accounts.name: trader_token
docs: account of the same mint as the vault.

types.name: ClearV2Output
docs: The output of the callback instruction. Provided as a struct with ordered fields
as anchor does not support tuples and tuple structs yet.

types.name: ClockAccount
docs: An account storing the current network epoch

types.name: ComputationDefinitionAccount
docs: An account representing a [ComputationDefinition] in a MXE.

types.name: ComputationDefinitionMeta
docs: A computation definition for execution in a MXE.

types.name: ComputationSignature
docs: The signature of a computation defined in a [ComputationDefinition].

types.name: Epoch
docs: The network epoch

types.name: InitBookOutput
docs: The output of the callback instruction. Provided as a struct with ordered fields
as anchor does not support tuples and tuple structs yet.

types.name: LeaderChoice
docs: The computation chosen by a node to be executed when the node is leader.

types.name: LeaderInfo
docs: The information about a node.

types.name: LeaderSelector
docs: To select a Leader.
Uses the greatest divisors method: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%27Hondt_method

types.name: MXEAccount
docs: A MPC Execution Environment.

types.name: MxeStatus
docs: The status of an MXE.

types.name: NodeMetadata
docs: location as [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://www.iso.org/iso-3166-country-codes.html) country code

types.name: NodeRef
docs: A reference to a node in the cluster.
The offset is to derive the Node Account.

types.name: OrderTicket
docs: One per order. Holds the public side of the order (who, and what they
deposited) and which encrypted-book slot it landed in.

types.name: Output
docs: An output of a computation.
We currently don't support encrypted outputs yet since encrypted values are passed via
data objects.

types.name: Parameter
docs: A parameter of a computation.
We differentiate between plaintext and encrypted parameters and data objects.
Plaintext parameters are directly provided as their value.
Encrypted parameters are provided as an offchain reference to the data.
Data objects are provided as a reference to the data object account.

types.name: PlaceOrderV2Output
docs: The output of the callback instruction. Provided as a struct with ordered fields
as anchor does not support tuples and tuple structs yet.

types.name: SetUnset
docs: Utility struct to store a value that needs to be set by a certain number of participants (keys
in our case). Once all participants have set the value, the value is considered set and we only
store it once.
